title: NPS vs Mutual Funds: Accessing Retirement Savings Before 60
description: The National Pension System (NPS) is primarily designed for long-term retirement savings with strict lock-in periods and specific withdrawal conditions until .

faq.q: Can I withdraw my entire NPS corpus before age 60?
faq.a: No, a premature exit from NPS before age 60 requires you to annuitise at least 80% of your corpus, with only 20% available as a taxable lump sum, provided you have subscribed for at least 10 years [cite: PFRDA].

faq.q: Are there any tax benefits for investing in mutual funds for retirement?
faq.a: While most mutual funds don't offer upfront tax deductions like NPS, Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) qualify for deductions under Section 80C with a three-year lock-in [cite: Income Tax India]. Long-term capital gains from equity funds also enjoy favourable tax treatment.

faq.q: How do partial withdrawals from NPS affect my retirement corpus?
faq.a: Partial withdrawals reduce your overall corpus, which will consequently lead to a smaller annuity and lump sum available at retirement. It's generally advisable to keep your retirement savings intact as much as possible.

faq.q: Is an ELSS fund the same as NPS in terms of lock-in?
faq.a: No, ELSS funds have a mandatory lock-in of three years from the date of investment for each contribution [cite: Income Tax India]. NPS, on the other hand, has a general lock-in till age 60, with very specific conditions for partial or premature withdrawals.

faq.q: What happens if I move abroad as an NRI? Can I continue my NPS account?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can open and operate NPS accounts. If you were a resident Indian and moved abroad, you can continue your existing NPS account as an NRI [cite: PFRDA].

faq.q: Can I switch between NPS and mutual funds?
faq.a: You cannot directly switch funds from NPS to a mutual fund scheme or vice-versa without exiting the respective scheme. Exiting NPS prematurely has significant restrictions and tax implications.
